reason: Conversation 2 got to the correct diagnosis efficiently: it ran a sensible cup-of-water test, then correctly read H98 as a high-voltage output fault requiring an engineer or Panasonic support, with consistent safety warnings about not opening the case. Conversation 1 never interpreted the H98 code, kept calling the appliance a 'Panasonic NNH98' even after the customer gave the real model NN-CD87KSBPQ, asked about low-power settings after the symptom was already clear, speculated about an overheat cut-out that doesn't fit the facts, and ignored the explicit 'is it worth fixing' question. Conversation 2's only weakness is treating 'NN-H98' as a model in its first reply and not discussing repair-vs-replace cost, but it still served the homeowner far better.
